title: How to Do the Dead Bug for Beginners (Ab Exercise Without Neck Pain)
intro: The dead bug is an ab exercise done lying on your back, moving opposite arms and legs. It trains your deep core muscles without straining your neck, so it's suitable for beginners.
muscles: Deep core muscles (transversus abdominis), front abs, hip muscles and arm-leg coordination. The dead bug strengthens your tummy, but doesn't burn belly fat specifically. Belly fat comes down when your whole body loses fat through eating and movement.
steps: Lie on your back, lift your arms straight up to the ceiling.
Lift your legs, knees bent 90 degrees above your hips.
Press your lower back flat onto the floor and keep it there.
Lower your right arm back behind your head and slowly straighten your left leg.
Breathe out, come back to the middle, then switch sides.
mistakes: Lower back lifting off the floor. Make the movement smaller until your back can stay flat.
Moving too fast. Take 2-3 seconds to lower and 2-3 seconds to come back.
Holding your breath. Breathe out each time your arm and leg go out.
easier: Move only your legs while your arms stay up, or tap your heels on the floor with your knees still bent.
harder: Straighten your leg lower, closer to the floor, or hold 3 seconds in the extended position before coming back.
dose: Beginner: 2-3 sets x 6-10 reps each side, rest 30-60 seconds. Do it 3 times a week.
safety: Stop if your lower back hurts or your tummy bulges up like a ridge in the middle. Mums who have just given birth or anyone with diastasis recti, hernia or chronic back pain should get advice from a doctor or physiotherapist first.

faq.q: Is the dead bug better than sit-ups?
faq.a: For beginners, the dead bug is easier to control and doesn't pull on your neck. It trains your tummy to stabilise your body, which is useful for carrying kids, grocery bags and so on.

faq.q: Can the dead bug get rid of a pot belly?
faq.a: It strengthens your ab muscles, but belly fat can't be burned from one spot. Combine exercise with suitable food portions, enough sleep and lots of walking, and fat will come off from your whole body, including your belly.

faq.q: Is it suitable for mums who just gave birth?
faq.a: The easy version is commonly used in postnatal recovery, but wait for your doctor's clearance first. If you see a bulge in the middle of your tummy, stop and see a women's health physiotherapist.
